source.title: Why Rectified Power Unit Networks Fail and How to Improve It: An Effective Field Theory Perspective

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. The supplied text includes the paper through its appendices.
record.tranche_reason: Tests how activation choice, initialization and residual architecture affect deep-network trainability, using kernel statistics and classification outcomes rather than the original studies’ methods.
record.gate_note: The paper reports initialization and training results for RePU and MRePU networks, including classification on MNIST and CIFAR-10. Results cited from prior work are not recorded as rows. CIFAR-10 test accuracies are not used as evidence for training error; rows use reported training accuracy or explicit divergence/stalling outcomes. Other reported CIFAR-10 results are omitted where they do not establish a training outcome tied to the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The initialization and training experiments test V4 through activation-dependent initialization, input scaling and trainable depth. CIFAR-10 training outcomes also bear on V1's allowance for substantial error under short, regularized training. The study does not test V3's depth-dependent plain-versus-residual comparison.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is broadly accurate. The authors show that RePU cannot simultaneously satisfy the two criticality conditions. MRePU permits an activation- and depth-dependent initialization rule whose guarantees concern infinite-width initialization statistics. It improves empirical trainability through 32 MNIST layers and across all tested PINN depths. CIFAR-10 success depends on architecture and activation-input scale, with seed failures and unstable BN evaluation in some settings. Improved trainability does not imply better accuracy or eventual near-zero training error.
record.recipe_differences: Studies RePU/MRePU activation and initialization rather than the original sources’ methods for generalization, residual learning, initialization, learning-rate stability or batch normalization. Uses synthetic regression, PINNs, MNIST and CIFAR-10 experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: MRePU CIFAR-10 outcome varied with residual architecture, initialization scale/input kernel, activation degree and learning rate; MNIST trainability varied with input scale, weight variance, depth and rescaled depth τ.

fits_no_version.finding: Empirical kernel magnitudes and NTK statistics at initialization characterize signal propagation but do not themselves measure learning speed or successful training.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: RePU initialization has unstable signal propagation; small-kernel MRePU initialization can preserve forward and gradient scales over a finite depth range.

fits_no_version.finding: NF-γ MRePU training recovers from transient loss spikes, without a measured learning-rate stability threshold or curvature trajectory.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Some unnormalized MRePU runs recover from large transient training-loss spikes.

fits_no_version.finding: BN-based MRePU networks can have unstable test loss despite increasing training accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: BN evaluation statistics can interact with RePU-type activation tails and produce unstable evaluation.

record.problems: CIFAR-10 training lasts only five epochs, so reported accuracy is not converged. CIFAR-10 results use three seeds per setting. MNIST short-run experiment uses three initializations; its trainability measure is test accuracy threshold rather than training error. Some kernel and phase-diagram results are figure-based.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted CIFAR-10 table rows for ReLU, GELU and SiLU, since they are reference activations rather than RePU/MRePU outcomes. Omitted detailed kernel trajectories during training and CIFAR-10 validation-selection results because corresponding settings are redundant with the retained condition groups or do not provide additional classification training-error evidence. Initialization kernel rows for RePU are retained as evidence relevant to V4.

untested.parts: Eventual near-zero training error with sufficient training; CIFAR-100; corrupted or random labels; unregularized SGD or Adam comparisons; a controlled model-size or stopping-time sweep. CIFAR-10 uses five-epoch AdamW training with weight decay and augmentation.
All parts: no two-layer ReLU teacher-student local-minimum or extra-neuron experiment.

All parts: no controlled depth sweep comparing plain batch-normalized convolutional networks with identity-shortcut counterparts, no longer-training control, and no tests of the specified tanh or Fixup exceptions.

The named original initialization schemes, orthogonal-versus-Gaussian tanh training, orthogonal convolution kernels and 10,000-layer training. Most retained outcomes measure whether learning occurs within a short budget rather than training speed at matched accuracy.
All parts: no initial linearized stability threshold, sharpness trajectory or controlled above-threshold learning-rate experiment.
All parts: the normalization comparisons do not isolate BN's speed or learning-rate advantage against otherwise matched unnormalized networks, and do not implement Fixup.

missing.what: Within-MRePU input-scale and weight-variance sweep: at depth 5 the divergence boundary follows the fixed-point curve, but standard-normalized inputs can diverge even with a decreasing initialization kernel.

Within-MRePU initialization-rule comparison: successful rescaled-depth ranges are ordered R1 > R3 > CW=1, and shrink with actual depth. Record success fractions or readable thresholds separately by depth and activation degree.

PINN trainability by PDE, depth and activation: all 72 MRePU runs remain trainable; RePU has at least two failures per PDE at depth 5 and non-finite initial loss for every seed at depth 7. Separate non-finite training loss from the table's relative-error-based divergence criterion.
missing.locator: Section 5.2, Table 7, Figure 15 and trainability summary

missing.what: Training accuracy comparisons omitted despite only test-accuracy baseline rows being declared omitted: trained MRePU has accuracy 0.70–0.74 versus ReLU 0.83–0.89, while GELU and SiLU in critical-scale variants remain below 0.67. Preserve the aggregate nature of these ranges.
missing.locator: Section 5.3.2, Results and Trainability and accuracy

record.verdict_notes: V3 verdicts should be removed: residual-network failures without a controlled depth comparison do not test its stated degradation effect. No verdict challenges eventual CIFAR interpolation because training is short and regularized. A single row state cannot fully describe both V1 fitting completeness and V4 trainability; rows with partial fitting but successful learning should be split by measure.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, SGD, or the full range of smaller models, early stopping and regularized recipes. CIFAR-10 runs last five epochs; MNIST runs last three epochs.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student experiments or neuron-count sweep.

Does not compare plain batch-normalized networks with residual networks at increasing depth on ImageNet or CIFAR-10. CIFAR-10 comparisons are among residual architectures and activations; synthetic regression includes fully connected networks, not convolutional networks.
Does not test the initialization schemes or plain tanh/convolutional networks named in the version. Tests RePU/MRePU initialization and kernel behavior, including CIFAR-10 residual settings.
No above-stability learning-rate or sharpness experiment.
Does not test batch normalization’s general speed or learning-rate tolerance against unnormalized counterparts, or Fixup as stated in the version.
